personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: A hand-rolled Mode 7 engine is a lot of new code in the arcade. Pure modules with a test on every rule is the only way I would trust it.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: A third arcade game is exactly the fluff that makes this look like a gimmick to me.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: A whole game from one idea, built by the loop: that is the speed I want to show the teams.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: It plugs in like the two games before it: the same registry, the same unlock, the same score path.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: No customer asked for a kart game. Fine as a reward for the team, but it is not a quick win for anyone we sell to.

objection.text: I already see omni-loop as a gimmick, fluff. A third game whose whole engine loads for everyone who opens the arcade, even without ever playing it, is exactly the fluff I mean.

personas.reaction: Every rule is a pure module with its test, a slow frame cannot push a kart through a wall, and the engine never loads on a page I work on.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: Still a game, but it costs nothing to anyone who never opens the cabinet, and it needs no migration.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: One circuit now and more later keeps it shippable in one PRD.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: Same registry, unlock and score path as PRD 817, every choice written in Decisions, and a guard on what loads when.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: Nothing here reaches a customer. I would rather the loop's time went to quick wins they feel.
